svg.title: Pocket Reader — Schematic
svg.desc: Complete schematic of the ESP32-C3 based e-paper reader: USB-C input, MCP73831 Li-Po charge circuit, TPS63020 3.3 V buck-boost, ESP32-C3-MINI-1, 24-pin e-paper FPC connector, buttons and battery sense divider.
svg.text: Rev 1.0 · ESP32-C3-MINI-1 · 2.13" e-paper (SSD1680, 250×122) · 1S Li-Po · USB-C 5 V · page 1/1
U1: in series with the D+ / D− lines
J1: A4/B4 VBUS · A5 CC1 · B5 CC2 · A6/B6 D+/D− · A1/B1/A12/B12 GND
If the cell has its own
GPIO2/GPIO8 are strapping pins: must be HIGH at boot; EPD_RST and button pull-ups ensure it.
Since GPIO9 = BUSY (HIGH when idle), the boot condition is met automatically as well.
GPIO20 = U0RXD → input only; the MENU button therefore cannot wake via GPIO.
Because GPIO6 (MTCK) is used, the JTAG line is unavailable — debug via USB-Serial-JTAG.
⚠️ Pinout verified. Remaining risk: external VGH/VGL boost circuit.
The panel builds its own ±15 V boost via GDR(2)/RESE(3) pins. In the first prototype
use a ready-made adapter board (docs/02 §F). Details: pinouts.md §1.
All buttons have 100nF hardware debounce + 100k pull-up. GPIO2/GPIO3 are in the RTC domain,
so they wake from deep sleep via ext1; GPIO20 cannot wake.
Resistors connect to the 3V3 rail, capacitors to GND (simplified in the schematic).
Divider ratio 1:2 → the actual battery voltage is 2× the measured voltage.
The divider's continuous current at 4.2 V is 21 µA; this is the dominant drain in sleep.
1M/1M can be used for lower drain (mind the ADC input impedance limit).
Alternative: MAX17048 I²C fuel gauge (if GPIO8/9 are free).
Blue label = net name (same name = connected)
Red box = information that must be verified
